history.summary: Built by Thakur Ani Nath Shahdeo, king of Barkagarh, and completed on 25 December 1691, this ~100-foot temple stands on a hillock at Jagannathpur, Dhurwa, about 10 km southwest of Ranchi city centre, in the Kalinga architectural style modelled on the Puri Jagannath Temple. A subsidiary shrine called Mausibadi sits on a nearby hill and receives the Rath Yatra procession each Ashadha (June/July). The original 1691 temple collapsed on 6 August 1990 and was rebuilt from 8 February 1992 with state-government and patron support. (verify) Wikipedia states the 1691 temple was desecrated by Aurangzeb; this claim rests on a single citation and should not be repeated as settled fact. The nearby 17th-century Sun Temple at Bundu (seq 401) is sometimes confused with it.

name: Jagannath Temple
town_description: Ranchi, the capital of Jharkhand, is a plateau city in the Chotanagpur region known for its waterfalls, hills, and tribal heritage. Dhurwa, where the temple stands, is a southwestern suburb of the city near the HEC industrial township.

travel.road: Via Jagannathpur Hill Road from Ranchi city; reachable by local taxis, autos, buses, then 200+ steps or a motorable route to the hilltop

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Rath Yatra in Ashadha (June-July) for the festival
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported as 5:30 AM-9:00 PM; hours vary across sources (verify locally)
